JVM specification: NEW bytecode instruction triggers class loading via ClassLoader.loadClass if the class is not already loaded

toolLimitation.reason: WALA abstracts away the JVM's class loading mechanism. When processing NEW instructions, WALA directly models the class initialization (<clinit>) via processClassInitializer() but does not model the implicit ClassLoader.loadClass() call that precedes class initialization in the actual JVM. The tool treats class loading as an implicit operation outside the call graph, directly connecting to <clinit> methods without modeling the ClassLoader invocation chain.

potentialTestCase.description: Create a minimal Java program with a main class that has a static initializer containing a NEW instruction for another class (e.g., static field initialized with new HelperClass()). The NEW instruction will trigger ClassLoader.loadClass() at runtime to load HelperClass before calling its <clinit>. WALA will model the <clinit> call but miss the ClassLoader.loadClass edge.
